# Working on herdr-orchestrators

This repo builds two ODD orchestrator agents, `hcorc` (Herdr desktop) and
`herdorc` (herdr terminal multiplexer), plus ten role agents, for several
coding CLIs. `README.md` describes the product; this file is for changing it.

## Sources and generated files

- Sources: `shared/` (core, docs, roles, skills, vendored herdr skill,
  `bin/orc.py`, `bin/guard.py`), `layers/` (per-orchestrator layers, shared
  section, slash-command templates), `mods/` (Claude Code-only plugins),
  `herdr-app/mods/` (Herdr desktop mods, for any CLI).
- Everything under `.claude/agents/`, `.claude/commands/` and every CLI's
  install location is generated by `install.py`. It writes the files into
  `dist/` (git-ignored; `$ORC_DIST` overrides it) and links each install
  location to them. Never edit generated files, nor the files behind the
  links; edit the source and regenerate. Shared files (`settings.json`
  hooks, Herdr layouts and `keys.json`, herdr's `config.toml`) are merged,
  never linked.
- Installing is `./install.sh` (every part the machine has) or
  `installers/<target>.sh` (one part). They are thin wrappers: the logic
  stays in `install.py` and `herdr-app/extras.py`. A new install option goes
  there, then into the wrapper's help and the README table.
- `shared/core`, `shared/docs`, `shared/roles` and most of `shared/skills`
  are ported from tomidev-shell by `scripts/port-*.py`, with every change
  recorded in `shared/PROVENANCE-*.md`. Change a ported text through its
  port script, so the provenance stays true.
- `herdr-app/patches/agent-flow/` patches the third-party Herdr app mod
  herdr-agent-flow so it draws `orc.py ensure --handoff` as a message. Its
  README names the agent-flow commit the patches are made against and how to
  reapply them after agent-flow is updated. Changing what `orc.py ensure`
  accepts (`--as`, `--name`, `--handoff`) needs the same change in the patch.

## Rules

- Keep prompts CLI-agnostic: say "ask tool", "subagent tool", "shell tool".
  `install.py` (`VOCAB`, `CLIS`) maps them per CLI. Put anything that only
  works where a CLI has hooks or slash commands in `<!-- if:hooks -->` or
  `<!-- if:commands -->` blocks. Only the mods in `mods/` may be specific to
  Claude Code.
- `orc.py` identifies the orchestrator from `--as <agent>` or
  `$CLAUDE_CODE_AGENT`. The mods read its files, so keep these stable:
  the phase file name and its `phase` key (`orc-cache`), the herdorc state
  file, and `~/.local/state/orc/reports` (`orc-graph`).
- `mods/orc-graph/hooks/roster.ts` and `mods/orc-context/hooks/roster.ts`
  duplicate `ROLES`, the role-name pattern, the herdorc state file path and
  `safe()` from `orc.py` / `orc_state.py`. A change there needs the same change
  in both copies.
- `herdr-app/mods/orc-skills` reads `orc.py skills --json`; keep its `conflicts`
  and `skills` keys stable. Run `herdr-app check herdr-app/mods/orc-skills`
  after changing it. Its layout node IDs (`orc-skills-bar`, `-toggle`,
  `-panel`) are shared with `install.py`; never edit Herdr's shipped layouts
  or mods (clone them).
- Tests and experiments never touch the user's terminals or sessions: use
  `HC_SESSION=<name>` for herdr-core and a named `herdr --session` for herdr.
- `herdr/plugins/orc-flow/` is a herdr plugin (Node, any CLI), ported from
  herdr-agent-flow (MIT; its licence is the plugin's `LICENSE`, its changes
  are listed in the plugin's README). It reads herdorc's state file and
  copies `ROLES` and the state file path rule from `shared/roles/roles.json`
  and `shared/bin/orc_state.py` into `lib/herdr.mjs`: a change there needs
  the same change in the plugin. It also reads `orc.py ensure ... --handoff`,
  the herdr commands herdorc's layer uses to prompt and read role panes, and
  report files named `<pane-name>-<task>.md`; keep them in step with
  `layers/herdorc.md`.
- `herdr-app/extras.json` pins each third-party Herdr app mod to a commit
  whose code was read. Bump a `ref` only after reading the new code, and
  check that `herdr-app/patches/agent-flow` still applies to a new agent-flow.
  Tests use `ORC_EXTRAS_SPEC` and `ORC_EXTRAS_SRC`, never the network.
- `herdr plugin link` writes to herdr's config, which every herdr session
  shares. Link the plugin for tests only in a herdr whose config is isolated
  (`XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<short dir>`, since herdr's socket path must stay short),
  with a named session.

## Commands

- Regenerate this repo's `.claude/`: `python3 scripts/build-agents.py`
- Install: `./install.sh --help`, `installers/<target>.sh --help`,
  `python3 install.py --help`
- Tests: `bash tests/test_install.sh` (self-contained), then
  `bash tests/test_guard.sh`, `bash tests/test_orc_herdr.sh`,
  `bash tests/test_orc_hc.sh` (need herdr / Herdr desktop).
- herdr skill drift: `python3 scripts/sync-herdr-skill.py`
- orc-flow plugin tests: `node --test herdr/plugins/orc-flow/test/`
